limitations: Local implementation and synthetic verification never approve a public or scientific release.
The Docker deployment assumes a trusted single host; internal service traffic is private, not mutually authenticated across untrusted hosts.
Backup keys and offsite copies require operator-managed protected storage and tested retention.
External SMTP, public identity recovery and independent domain/legal/security sign-offs remain separate evidence gates.
Public requests admitted before a pause may finish within their existing deadline; private RPC/administrator tools remain privileged diagnostics.
Restored bucket is isolated; real target-host cutover and storage policy/credential reapplication require the runbook.
Original source/calculation/alert timestamps, policy/code hashes and scientific approval are never renewed by restore/replay.
